data.title: Canonical URL
data.tagline: A preferred representative URL for pages with the same or very similar content
data.learningOutcome: You can choose a representative URL and distinguish a canonical hint from a redirect that changes the address bar.
data.description: Several product URLs with campaign parameters can remain accessible while each page declares a parameter-free representative URL in its head and the sitemap lists that same address. A canonical is usually a hint to search systems, not a browser redirect; use a redirect when visitors must move.

learning.assumes: You have seen product or article URLs with query parameters and know that a page can contain link metadata in its head.
learning.outcome: You can choose a representative URL and distinguish a canonical hint from a redirect that changes the address bar.

explanation.title: A page declares its preferred representative
explanation.text: A page with parameters or another duplicate entry can use rel=canonical in its head to point to the URL it prefers search systems to recognize as representative.

explanation.title: The visited URL and representative can differ
explanation.text: People may still open the parameterized current URL, and the address bar normally does not change because of canonical. The sitemap should use the chosen representative too.

data.boundary: A canonical is a hint about which URL should represent a group to search systems. A redirect sends a visit from an old URL to a new one. Canonical usually does not change the address bar and is not a forced command; use a redirect when people must leave the old URL.

lessonPractice.title: Visitors must automatically reach the new product URL instead of staying on the old one. What should be used?

options.label: Configure a redirect from the old URL to the new one and check that the address bar changes
options.feedback: Correct. When visitors must reach a new address, use and verify a redirect; a canonical hint normally does not change the address bar.

options.label: Add only a canonical link to the new URL in the old page head
options.feedback: A canonical is a preferred-version hint, and the old URL usually remains accessible. It does not by itself migrate visitors.

options.label: Delete the old page and let it show a not-found page
options.feedback: Deleting the old URL creates a 404 without sending visitors to the new content or preserving a migration relationship.

data.agentPrompt: Set the no-parameter product URL as the canonical in the head of parameterized pages, and list only that main URL in sitemap.xml. Check each page's canonical, the sitemap list, and the browser address bar to confirm that canonical does not automatically redirect the parameterized page.

references.title: How to specify a canonical URL
